title: Minimum Cost to Acquire Required Items
summary: Given five integers cost1, cost2, costBoth, need1, and need2, determine the minimum cost to acquire enough items of three types to meet the requirements of at least need1 units of type 1 and need2 units of type 2.
statement: Given five integers cost1, cost2, costBoth, need1, and need2, determine the minimum cost to acquire enough items of three types to meet the requirements of at least need1 units of type 1 and need2 units of type 2. Each type 1 item costs cost1, each type 2 item costs cost2, and each type 3 item costs costBoth but contributes to both types. The cost of type 3 items is shared between the two types.
constraints: Costs are positive and needs are nonnegative integers.
A both-item contributes one unit toward each requirement.
Requirements are lower bounds, so buying extra of one type is allowed.
hints: For a chosen number k of both-items, remaining needs are max(0,need1-k) and max(0,need2-k).
This piecewise-linear cost can change slope only at zero, min(need1,need2), or max(need1,need2).
Evaluate no both-items, exactly the shared minimum, and enough both-items for both requirements.
Between breakpoints the cost is linear, so an interval minimum occurs at an endpoint; these three plans cover every endpoint.
editorial: Between breakpoints the cost is linear, so an interval minimum occurs at an endpoint; these three plans cover every endpoint.

tests.explanation: Three both-items cost three and satisfy both lower bounds.
Separate items cost twenty-two, cheaper than any both-item plan.
